MXene Atlas — an evidence-linked map of MXene propertiesv2

What has been built so far — each round: what it measured and how it ended · «undecidable» is not failure but «to be filled when data arrives»
Values extracted from open-access experimental papers · one dot = one sample under one condition · click a dot to see the source sentence · measurement conditions differ, so do not compare values directly
⚠️ Not “verified” yet — values were checked against the source by two AI judges only (no human check yet). The “strict” tab filters on machine-extracted fact fields, and the accuracy of that filter has not been measured (the test stopped as undecidable for lack of samples · Oct 8).
Etchant question — cations from fluoride-salt etching (NH₄HF₂·NH₄F·NaF·KF) are treated as part of etching, like LiF/HCl samples, and stay in the strict tab · TMAOH is a deliberate intercalant and is excluded · basis = Gogotsi-lab reviews and protocol papers (to be revisited when outside experts reply)
Structure view — ① click an element in the periodic table to filter → ② in the network (3D · drag to rotate · wheel to zoom) click a paper dot to see its values and source → ③ click a property dot to jump to “Find by target value” below · follows the sample tab and etchant-question answer below

Loading the network… (needs internet — the 3D library comes from a public CDN)
● Blue = which MXene (composition · e.g. Ti₃C₂ · V₂C)● Orange = which etchant (etching · e.g. HF · LiF/HCl)● Pink = how layers were separated (delamination · capacitance data only · skipped when not stated)● Grey = sample form (e.g. free-standing film · film on substrate · electrode · powder)● Green = what was measured (property, by unit · e.g. conductivity S/cm · capacitance F/g · shielding dB)● Small purple dot = one source paper (hover for its ID · click for source sentences)Thicker lines = more values connecting the two · How to read: paths run composition → etchant → delamination → form → property · a thick “Ti₃C₂ — LiF/HCl — free-standing film — S/cm” path means many conductivity values for LiF/HCl-etched Ti₃C₂ made into free-standing films

Ask — if you need this property, which MXene was made, and how?
How to use: ① click an example below or ② type a question (e.g. «high conductivity MXene» · «large surface area» · «low work function») → it recognises the property and «high/low», gathers samples in the top 10% (bottom 10% for «low») of that property, and counts which etchant and which form they were made with. Version 2 (10/9): also understands conditions — etchant (LiF/HCl · HF · fluoride salt · molten salt) · «non-Ti» · a composition (e.g. Nb2C) · «film». v3 (10/9 afternoon): conditions can be combined — element names (vanadium · niobium · molybdenum …) · delamination (TMAOH · sonication · shaking) · «pure» (no mixed material) · form (powder · aerogel · fiber · free-standing film) · add «compare» to get a table of values, papers and median per etching route.
Examples
The answer appears here — it is a list of source candidates («samples made this way reached this value»), not a guarantee that «making it this way gives this value».
Find by target value — how were the samples that reached it made?
How to use: ① pick a property in the «Unit» row above → ② type the value you need → ③ «Find». Samples that reached it are grouped by etchant; click a line to see the source sentence.
at leastFollows the sample tab, unit and etchant-question answer chosen above · conditions differ, so this does not promise “this method gives this value” — it is a list of candidates to check in the source
Enter a target value and press “Find” to list the samples that reached it, grouped by etchant.
Same recipe, different values — how much do values differ between papers for samples with the same composition, etchant, delamination and form?
Uses the unit and sample tab above · one vote per paper (its median) · values judged wrong ✕ excluded · groups with ≥2 papers only · largest spread first · click a row to compare the highest and lowest source sentences side by side — the cause may be conditions not in these fields (thickness, method, post-treatment, oxidation) · this shows where to look, not the cause
